clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis caused by biallelic FAN1 variants; FAN1 encodes a DNA interstrand-crosslink repair nuclease.
Defined histologically by karyomegaly, that is strikingly enlarged, hyperchromatic and bizarre nuclei, of renal tubular epithelial cells.
Presents insidiously with progressive chronic kidney disease, usually detected in early-to-mid adulthood.
Urinalysis typically shows a bland sediment with modest tubular proteinuria and little or no haematuria.
Recurrent respiratory tract infections are a frequently reported association.
Karyomegaly is a systemic finding, also affecting liver, lung and neurons, although the clinical picture is renal-predominant.
The underlying DNA-repair defect confers heightened cellular sensitivity to genotoxic agents and a possible predisposition to malignancy.
Diagnosis requires renal biopsy and is confirmed by FAN1 molecular genetic testing.
reference.pathophysiology: FAN1 on chromosome 15q13.3 encodes the FANCD2/FANCI-associated nuclease 1, a structure-specific DNA nuclease that acts in the repair of DNA interstrand crosslinks and in the protection and restart of stalled replication forks, working in concert with the Fanconi anaemia pathway. Biallelic loss-of-function variants leave cells unable to repair crosslink damage, so they accumulate DNA lesions and undergo repeated rounds of DNA replication without completing mitosis (endoreduplication), generating the polyploid, grossly enlarged karyomegalic nuclei that are the histological signature of the disease. This damage is most conspicuous in renal tubular epithelium, where progressive tubular injury drives chronic interstitial inflammation, tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis, and hence slowly progressive chronic kidney disease; the same repair defect underlies the reported sensitivity to genotoxic agents and the concern about cancer risk.
additionalDifferentials: Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease (UMOD, MUC1, REN, HNF1B)
Analgesic nephropathy and aristolochic acid or Balkan endemic nephropathy
Chronic lithium and other drug-induced tubulointerstitial nephritis
Viral cytopathic change (cytomegalovirus, BK polyomavirus, adenovirus) mimicking karyomegaly
additionalInvestigations: Renal biopsy with light microscopy for karyomegaly, interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy
Immunohistochemistry or in-situ studies to exclude viral inclusions
Serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate
Careful drug and environmental or toxin exposure history
Molecular genetic testing of FAN1 with screening of relatives
redFlags: Progressive decline in renal function towards end-stage
Features of advanced chronic kidney disease
Signs suggesting malignancy, given the DNA-repair defect
reference.prognosis: The disease is progressive and most affected individuals reach end-stage renal disease requiring dialysis or transplantation by mid-adulthood; kidney transplantation is feasible as the defect does not recur in the graft.
pitfalls: Frequently dismissed as chronic interstitial nephritis of unknown cause when no biopsy is performed.
Karyomegaly can be mistaken for a viral cytopathic effect or for malignancy.
Genotoxic chemotherapy and other DNA-damaging agents should be used with particular caution.
Affected relatives may be undiagnosed and warrant screening.
references: Reviews of hereditary tubulointerstitial kidney disease
management: Slow chronic kidney disease progression with blood-pressure control and renin-angiotensin-system blockade, as no disease-specific therapy exists
Avoid nephrotoxic drugs and adjust medication doses to renal function
Manage complications of chronic kidney disease including anaemia, metabolic acidosis and mineral-bone disorder
Treat recurrent respiratory tract infections, a recognised association
Plan and initiate renal replacement therapy, with transplantation feasible as the defect does not recur in the graft
Provide genetic counselling and family screening for this autosomal recessive FAN1 disorder with ongoing nephrology follow-up
